evidence.experimental_conditions: Reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) treated with cinnamyl alcohol (1, 1a, 1b, 1c) for 1, 8, and 24 h; analyzed by 1D 13C HRMAS NMR and 2D 1H-13C g-HSQC NMR.
evidence.support_text: When cinnamyl alcohol 1a was incubated on RHE for 1, 8, and 24 h and analyzed by 1D 13C-HRMAS NMR, no signal at 200.6 ppm corresponding to cinnamaldehyde 2a was detected, even after 24 h of incubation. This was confirmed by 2D 1H-13C g-HSQC HRMAS NMR experiments where signals from cinnamaldehyde were never observed, indicating that cinnamyl alcohol is not oxidized to cinnamaldehyde in reconstructed human epidermis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) treated with cinnamyl alcohol isotopomers (1a, 1b, 1c) for 1, 8, and 24 h; analyzed by 2D 1H-13C g-HSQC HRMAS NMR at 500 MHz.

The 13C upfield chemical shift of 45.6 ppm is associated with attachment to a sulfur atom, demonstrating covalent conjugation of cinnamyl alcohol with a thiol nucleophile from glutathione or protein in the epidermis.

evidence.support_text: In the present study, splenocytes from SMX-NO-treated rats (1 mg/kg) showed a concentration-dependent proliferative response upon in vitro restimulation with 5-50 µM SMX-NO, as measured by [3H]thymidine incorporation. These concentrations caused low levels of cellular haptenation without reducing viability. Higher concentrations (100-250 µM) caused toxicity and inhibited proliferation. Additionally, SMX-NO-modified naive irradiated splenocytes stimulated proliferation of sensitized T cells, and the response was MHC-restricted.
